reasoning: Seedling stem with dark brown-to-black necrosis at the hypocotyl/soil-line region, transitioning through tan/yellow to healthy green tissue below. Lateral roots are dead and shriveled. This soft, water-soaked, near-black stem collapse in a young seedling is characteristic of Pythium damping-off. Rhizoctonia was considered but typically produces a more reddish-brown 'wire stem' lesion rather than the black, wet rot seen here.
